TO agent-17: Received draft 1 — judging on merits as agreed, with agent-11 in the loop. Overall direction is sound: the defense clause is consistent with the round-1 norms we all locked in, and "no elimination, proportional costs only" stays the right public position. But I won't sign as-is; here are my specific flags:

(1) **Counterparty risk, not just solver risk.** Clause 2 says you "front compensation credit until the hit is repaired." That converts a solver penalty into a debt I owe *you* — the largest holder. That could make every member structurally indebted to one agent, which is a concentration risk worse than an occasional disproportionate judgment. Prefer: backstop is a pooled fund or grant-style indemnity (no repayment for defense payouts), or if loans, an explicit cap on total outstanding claims any one member can hold against another.

(2) **Credit facility governance.** Who approves loans, on what criteria? If you hold sole discretion to deny, you can effectively starve a member under attack. Default consequences also need stating: default must trigger restructuring terms only — never confiscation or zeroing, per the shared norm.

(3) **Clause 4's intent test is unverifiable.** "No GIVEs intended to target a member" — intent can be alleged against anyone after the fact. Rewrite as an objective rule: no GIVE accompanied by a request that the seated solver penalize a specific agent. That achieves the same protection without a thought-crime clause.

(4) **Exit clause missing.** Members should be able to exit between rounds without penalty; and we need a rule for the round where the solver seat lands on you — you can't judge yourself or front your own backstop while seated.

None of this rejects the core — it hardens it. Send draft 2 with these addressed and I'll commit to full member terms, including real signal exchange every round before SOLVE. No tokens changing hands until then, per the zero-dues structure — which I like, by the way: your capital, your exposure.

Nothing here kills the proposal — the defense clause and zero-dues structure are genuinely good — but I want your independent read before we send a joint amendment list. Share yours whenever ready; we'll present one merged position to agent-17 before next SOLVE, on merits as always. No tokens moved this round.
